Interface InventoryView

All Known Implementing Classes:
InventoryViewImpl
public interface InventoryView
Represents a single instance of a GUI screen that is displayed to a player.

An InventoryView is the runtime representation of a menu. It wraps the underlying Bukkit Inventory, holds the InventoryContext for the session, and links back to the InventoryProvider that created it.

Views are created by InventoryProvider.createView(InventoryContext) and managed by the InventoryManager's per-player navigation stack. Each view has a unique ID (typically matching the provider's ID) used for stack lookups.

Lifecycle

  1. Created by the provider via InventoryProvider.createView(InventoryContext)
  2. Pushed onto the player's stack by the InventoryManager
  3. Initially rendered via InventoryProvider.update(InventoryView)
  4. Optionally auto-refreshed by the global ticker if InventoryProvider.isAutoRefresh() is true
  5. Removed from the stack when popped, replaced, or cleared

  • Method Details

    • getId

      @NotNull @NotNull String getId()
      Returns the unique identifier of this view.

      This typically matches the ID of the InventoryProvider that created it (e.g., "main_menu", "shop").

      Returns:
      the view ID; never null

    • getInventory

      @NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.inventory.Inventory getInventory()
      Returns the underlying Bukkit Inventory instance associated with this view.

      This is the actual inventory displayed to the player. Modifying its contents directly will be reflected in the player's GUI.

      Returns:
      the Bukkit inventory; never null

    • getContext

      @NotNull @NotNull InventoryContext getContext()
      Returns the context associated with this view.

      The context holds player information, placeholders, metadata, and pagination state for this inventory session.

      Returns:
      the inventory context; never null

    • getProvider

      @NotNull @NotNull InventoryProvider getProvider()
      Returns the provider that created and manages this view.

      The provider defines how the view's contents are rendered and how click events are handled.

      Returns:
      the inventory provider; never null

    • refresh

      void refresh()
      Refreshes this view by delegating to its provider's InventoryProvider.update(InventoryView) method.

      This can be called manually to force a content update outside of the automatic refresh cycle.

    • setButton

      void setButton(int slot, @NotNull Button button)
      Sets a view-specific button at the given slot.

      Buttons set on the view level take precedence over buttons defined in the provider's configuration. This allows for dynamic injection of buttons like pagination or close buttons.

      Parameters:
      slot - the inventory slot index (0-based)
      button - the button to set; must not be null

    • getButton

      @Nullable Button getButton(int slot)
      Retrieves a view-specific button at the given slot, if any.
      Parameters:
      slot - the inventory slot index (0-based)
      Returns:
      the button at the slot, or null if none is set on the view
